scope.description: Bounded, deterministic probe of whether a lost follower Accepted reply is repaired by the protocol's own resend/retry machinery within a window of 100 resend periods, or only by an unrelated later proposal.
assumptions: 2-node cluster so the write quorum is the leader's own acceptance plus exactly one follower receipt: one dropped message is enough to hide the quorum from the leader
error-free memory storage, FIFO delivery of everything else, no reordering, no crash and no leadership change during the window
one logical step per node equals one tick(), so the 500-step window contains 100 of the configured 5-tick resend periods for both roles

basis.prefix: Deterministic in-process simulation of the core crate: two real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2; configuration_id 1; MemoryStorage; error-free storage) built by OmniPaxosConfig::build, never run concurrently - the harness drives them manually: each step calls tick() on both, drains take_outgoing_messages() into a FIFO, and delivers every message to the receiver's handle_incoming, except that it deliberately discards exactly one PaxosMsg::Accepted (the follower's receipt). Node 1 has leader_priority 1 so the election is deterministic; election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1. Case lost_accepted_leaves_entry_undecided: elect (both nodes Leader/Follower in the accept phase), append one entry at the leader, drop the follower's Accepted, then run 100 resend periods of ticks (500 steps) with everything else delivered; it emits CA_EVENT lost_accepted_window {steps,resend_periods,produced,dropped,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx,follower_accepted_idx,follower_holds_undecided_entry,leader_still_stable} and asserts exactly one Accepted was dropped, the follower really holds the entry as Undecided at index 0 with accepted_idx 1, the leader and the follower are both still at decided index 0, and the leader is still the stable leader. It then appends a second entry on the same state and emits CA_EVENT later_proposal_repairs {steps_until_decided,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx}. Case delivered_accepted_decides is the control: identical, the receipt is delivered, and the entry must be decided inside the same bounded window (CA_EVENT delivered_accepted_decides). The prerequisite the probe relies on is not 'some message was dropped' but the actual per-message operands: which message kinds were produced and which was discarded are printed in the event.

Source: drain_notifiers resolves a pending call by matching the recorded assignment in the order `Some((idx, _)) if idx <= decided` first and `Some((idx, ballot)) if ballot < cur_ballot` second (actor.rs:201-222), i.e. as soon as the node's decided index covers the index the call was assigned, the call resolves Ok(idx) without checking that the entry at that index is the one the call submitted; the Superseded arm exists for the leadership-change case and its own documentation admits the entry may still be lost (event.rs:45-60), while the Ok contract is to await the entry's decided log index (handle.rs:114-137). Execution bd165f9c43d94a7c9b57791a1979c00b (experiment dcb373d7a7c843d981030cdf4ec8d37a-experiment, exit 0, its single test passed) ran the construction and parsed event 1 `overwritten_index_resolution`: {a_decided_idx: 1, a_entry_at_index_1_is_own: false, b_decided_idx: 1, b_idx: 1, resolution: "Ok(1)"}. Read operand-by-operand: node 1's call for its own entry resolved Ok(1) (resolution "Ok(1)"), node 1's decided index was 1 (a_decided_idx 1), the entry at index 1 on node 1 was NOT the entry that call submitted (a_entry_at_index_1_is_own false), and the entry that actually occupies index 1 is node 2's, which node 2's own call got assigned the same index for (b_idx 1, b_decided_idx 1). So the declared comparison holds: the completion endpoint reported success at an index whose decided entry is a different entry, and the Superseded heuristic written for that leadership change never fired because the index-based arm is matched first. The remaining premise the construction supplies rather than assumes: node 1 really held its own entry at index 1 before being re-synchronized (the harness reads it back as Undecided at that point) and node 2's log was empty when it took over (node 1 was isolated in both directions so its entry could not be adopted); both are harness-side preconditions of the interleaving, not target behaviors. Formal support is withheld for one reason: this receipt has parsing_error_count 1 - the companion `after_b_takeover` line rendered Rust's `{:?}` of Option<(u64,bool)>, which is not JSON, and was recorded as invalid_observation at event index 0 - so the account is 'explained' rather than a citation-backed 'holds' until the revised emission is executed; event 0 is deliberately not cited. Counter-limitations kept in force: (a) the interleaving is constructed, not sampled, and its frequency in a deployment is not measured; (b) the call is only wrong if the caller treats Ok(idx) as 'my entry is decided at idx', which is what the handle documentation and the crate's own usage example state ('durably decided at log idx'); the actor cannot verify identity here because Entry is only Clone + Debug, so the fix would have to keep the index-based success arm honest by another means (e.g. reporting Superseded whenever the assignment's ballot is no longer current) rather than by comparing values; (c) the case needs the assigned index to be overwritten while the call is still pending, which requires the caller's entry not to be replicated and a leader change before the deadline.
